classification.difficultyReason: Several linked decisions using the demonstrated definitions or procedures. Parts (c) and (d) of the complement example compute these two expressions separately and obtain different sets.

content.prompt:
True or False? Let $A$ and $B$ be sets in a universal set $U$.

$A\cap\overline B=B\cap\overline A$.

answer.worked:
False. The left side contains elements in $A$ only; the right contains elements in $B$ only. For $U=\{1\}$, $A=\{1\}$ and $B=\varnothing$,
$$\begin{align*}A\cap\overline B&=\{1\},\\B\cap\overline A&=\varnothing.\end{align*}$$
